items_missed: No agenda statement — 'see if you have a few minutes' is a time check, not 'I'll gather details then walk you through pricing, about 10-15 minutes'

Never asked box count, packing needs, storage stops, additional stops, or additional rooms (garage, balcony) — the customer volunteered at the end that it is 'one twin bed, 2 bikes, everything else is boxes,' which he never surfaced himself
What's-included list never given — no gas, truck, taxes, insurance, pads, bands, or tools mentioned at any point
No Worries $2,000 damage coverage never mentioned
No 'pricing is super simple' opener and no full no-hidden-fees pitch (no credit card fees / no fuel surcharge / no assembly fees)
Never explained that the clock starts on-site when the contract opens
No sense-check after the pricing and clock explanation
Save Your Ass only partially delivered — got 'the more prepared you are, the less time it takes, the less money you spend' but no consolidation examples and no carload tip
No bolded-details framing for the email, no 'reply with any corrections'
No 'any other questions before I let you go?' — and when she said she had a better quote elsewhere, no attempt to ask what she was comparing against or to re-frame on value
Branch hours and callback number never given
top_strength: The estimate itself was the sharp part: he gave a real 2.5-3.5 hour range for a one-bedroom with two movers, then explicitly flagged that the fourth-floor elevator at load-up would likely push it toward the high end, and priced both ends ($520 and $728) so she could see the spread. He also stayed patient and pleasant through her reception dropouts and a mid-call work interruption.
coaching_note: He lost this one on differentiators, not price — No Worries coverage, Meet Your Mover, the On-Time Guarantee, and the what's-included list were all skipped, so when she said 'I got a better quote somewhere else' there was nothing on the table but an hourly rate. Give the value pitch before the number, and when a customer says a competitor beat you, ask what they quoted before letting the call end.
phone_presence_notes: Warm and easy throughout — 'Love to hear it,' 'For sure,' zero friction when she needed a minute mid-call, and a genuinely gracious exit after losing the sale.
audio_review_reason: Short call with repeated reception breakup on the customer's side and a mid-call interruption — the transcript gives limited signal on whether the warmth in his word choice carried in actual tone.
